claims: The CDC recommends an updated 2025–2026 COVID-19 vaccine for people ages 6 months and older to protect against severe illness, hospitalization, and death.
The CDC recommends an annual flu vaccine for everyone 6 months and older.
An RSV vaccine is recommended for adults 75 and older, adults 50–74 with higher risk conditions, and pregnant people to protect infants.
HPV vaccine is routinely recommended for children aged 11–12.
HPV vaccine is available through age 26.
Tdap/Td protects against tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis (whooping cough).
The Shingrix vaccine is recommended for adults 50 and older.
Initial doses of Hepatitis B, DTaP, Hib, Pneumococcal (PCV), Polio, and Rotavirus are given to babies 0–6 months.
MMR and Varicella doses are typically given at 12–15 months.
Boosters for DTaP, Polio, MMR, and Varicella are given at 4–6 years.
Tdap, HPV, and Meningococcal vaccines are given at 11–12 years.
Routine child vaccinations (1994-2023) are estimated to have prevented 508 million illnesses.
Routine child vaccinations (1994-2023) are estimated to have saved 1.1 million lives.
Vaccines are available at pharmacies like CVS and Walgreens, healthcare provider offices, and health departments.
